transcript.content: Hello. What brings you into the clinic today?

Hi, Doctor. Um, well, I hope I'm not taking up your time with something silly, but... I guess what really brought me in is just a little issue I've been having at home. It's nothing major, and it's certainly not that I don't care, I promise I do. But... my wife will be telling me about things—like my cousin’s appointments or who's giving him rides—and I’m looking right at her, you know, trying to be a good husband. But then a minute later, I realize I didn’t actually take in half of what she just said. 

I feel terrible about it, to be honest, because I really am trying to listen. Is that... does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining it okay.
How long have you noticed this difficulty with paying attention?

Well, um... I guess it's been noticeably harder for about, oh, maybe 11 months now? Give or take. It really started standing out after my cousin moved in with us. He had surgery, you see, and we wanted to help him out. It's been wonderful having him, really, but... I suppose there's just been a lot more to keep track of since then. I hope that's not a bad thing to say. I just mean, with the extra schedules and all, I think I've been slipping up a bit more. Does that sound like a normal thing to happen when things get a little busier at home?
Did you have any trouble with paying attention or staying organized when you were a child or in school?

Oh, um... well, I hope you don't think I was a bad student or a troublemaker. I always tried my very best and respected my teachers, I promise. But... yes, I suppose if I think way back to grade school, definitely before I was 12, my teachers used to tell my parents that I was a bright boy. Which was very kind of them to say! 

But they... they did also mention that I was always daydreaming a bit. And I'd accidentally leave my homework in my desk, or I'd need a little extra reminding to finish my classwork. Just innocent mistakes, really, not because I didn't care or wanted to be difficult. I just had my head in the clouds sometimes, I guess. Is that... is that the sort of thing you're asking about? I hope I'm giving you the right kind of information.
Do you find yourself spending a lot of time worrying about many different everyday matters, to the point where it feels hard to control?

Oh, no, I wouldn't say I worry all that much. I mean, everyone has a little bit of stress, right? Especially when you're trying to take good care of your family. But I don't think it's anything out of the ordinary, and it certainly doesn't feel out of control. I always try to look on the bright side of things and just take it one day at a time. I hope that's the kind of answer you were looking for? I just want to make sure I'm not making a bigger deal out of things than I should be.

latest_inference.note: Ruled out F41.1 as the patient denies excessive or uncontrollable worry.
